item.title: Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing
item.description:
This workflow processes raw text-format (.txt) CV data exported from CHI (CH Instruments) electrochemical workstations. It automatically identifies test parameters, splits the continuous test curve into individual cycles, precisely aligns and pairs the data according to scan direction (forward/reverse), and exports the results as structured Excel spreadsheets.

This workflow serves as the data foundation for all subsequent CV analysis workflows.

Procedure

  1. Select the input folder: Use the file picker to select the folder containing the .txt raw data files exported from the electrochemical workstation.
  2. After automatic processing is complete, the output folder will be displayed in the interface and can be opened directly by clicking on it.
  3. An overlaid plot of the last-cycle CV curves at each scan rate is also generated automatically for a quick preview of data quality.

Data Format

You should select a folder containing the raw data files for each scan rate. Each raw data file follows a format similar to:

Nov. 11, 2025 15:18:24
Cyclic Voltammetry
File: d:\cv-1.bin
Data Source: Experiment
Instrument Model: CHI760F
4-electrode
Header:
Note:
Init E (V) = 0
High E (V) = 0.4
Low E (V) = 0
Init P/N = P
Scan Rate (V/s) = 1
Segment = 12
Sample Interval (V) = 0.001
Quiet Time (sec) = 2
Sensitivity (A/V) = 1e-4
Results:
Channel 1:
Segment 1:
Segment 2:
Segment 3:
Segment 4:
Segment 5:
Segment 6:
Segment 7:
Segment 8:
Segment 9:
Segment 10:
Segment 11:
Segment 12:
Potential/V, Current/A
0.000, -4.207e-6
0.001, -3.163e-6
0.002, -2.341e-6
0.003, -1.676e-6
0.004, -1.170e-6
0.005, -6.959e-7
0.006, -2.214e-7
0.007, 1.898e-7
0.008, 6.326e-7
0.009, 1.075e-6
0.010, 1.455e-6

Scientific Principles and Processing Logic

CV Scan Segmentation Principle

Cyclic voltammetry characterizes electrochemical behavior by applying a triangular potential waveform to the working electrode. A complete cycle typically consists of two scan segments:

  1. Forward Scan: The potential increases in the positive direction, corresponding to the anodic process.
  2. Reverse Scan: The potential decreases in the negative direction, corresponding to the cathodic process.

Cycle Splitting

Scan direction changes are identified by detecting turning points in the potential sequence. A data point is identified as a turning point when the potential EiE_iEi​ satisfies the following condition:

Ei≈Ehigh  or  Ei≈Elow,(Ei−Ei−1)⋅(Ei+1−Ei)≤0E_i \approx E_{\text{high}} \;\text{or}\; E_i \approx E_{\text{low}}, \quad (E_i - E_{i-1}) \cdot (E_{i+1} - E_i) \leq 0Ei​≈Ehigh​orEi​≈Elow​,(Ei​−Ei−1​)⋅(Ei+1​−Ei​)≤0

Endpoint Completion: Due to hardware sampling rate limitations, the last recorded data point may not have fully reached the set EhighE_{\text{high}}Ehigh​ or ElowE_{\text{low}}Elow​. The system automatically performs mathematical interpolation to ensure each scan segment lies within the strictly defined potential window [Elow, Ehigh][E_{\text{low}},\, E_{\text{high}}][Elow​,Ehigh​], thereby eliminating systematic errors in subsequent integration calculations caused by inconsistent windows.

Data Alignment and Closure

To ensure curve continuity, the system implements cross-scan alignment:

  • Ensures that the endpoint of the preceding scan segment coincides with the starting point of the following scan segment in physical space.
  • In Full Cycles mode, forces the data to start and close at the lowest potential, enabling direct use for plotting or integration calculations.

Output File Structure

The output Excel files (one .xlsx file per original .txt file) contain three worksheets:

Metadata

Records the original test conditions for the sample, including:

Parameter Description Unit
init_e Initial potential V
high_e / low_e Upper/lower limits of the potential window V
scan_rate Scan rate V/s
sample_interval Sample interval V

Full_Cycles

Data arranged by complete cycle, with each cycle containing a full forward scan and reverse scan. Used for plotting multi-cycle overlaid CV curves and observing cycling stability.

Scans_Split

Forward scans and reverse scans are fully separated, formatted as C{n}_forward and C{n}_reverse. This worksheet is the core input data for subsequent analysis workflows such as CV: Coulombic Efficiency and Capacitance Calculation, CV/Pseudocapacitance Analysis: b-Value Kinetic Analysis, and CV/Cdl: Double-Layer Capacitance and Electrochemically Active Surface Area Analysis.

FAQ

  • Scientific notation: The system automatically recognizes current values in scientific notation formats such as 1.0e-03.
  • Incomplete cycles: If a cycle is incomplete (containing only a unidirectional scan), the system retains and marks that segment without affecting the normal processing of the remaining cycles.

item.title: EIS Extraction: CHI Instruments Data Preprocessing
item.description:
If you have just received raw .txt files exported from a CHI electrochemical workstation and are not sure where to begin, this workflow is the right starting point.

It automatically converts the raw EIS text into standardized tables (*_eis.csv) and fills in the key columns needed for subsequent plotting and fitting. You do not need to rename columns manually or worry about minor differences between export formats.

What You Get

  • One *_eis.csv file per sample
  • Unified fields: freq_hz, z_real_ohm, z_imag_ohm, z_mod_ohm, phase_deg
  • Invalid data automatically removed (e.g., non-positive frequencies, empty values)
  • Automatically sorted by frequency from high to low, ready for direct use in Nyquist/Bode/DRT workflows

Procedure

  1. Select the input folder: choose the directory containing the raw CHI .txt EIS files.
  2. The system traverses all .txt files in the directory and processes them one by one.
  3. On completion, an xxx-eis-extract output folder is created alongside the input directory.

If a file has an unexpected format, the system skips it with a warning and continues processing the remaining files.

Data Recognition Logic (Brief)

The program first locates the Freq/Hz header row, then automatically matches columns from common aliases:

  • Frequency column: Freq/Hz / Frequency/Hz / f/Hz
  • Real-part column: Z'/ohm / Zreal/ohm / Z'/Ω
  • Imaginary-part column: Z"/ohm / Z''/ohm / Zimag/ohm

From these, it computes:

∣Z∣=Z′2+Z′′2,ϕ=arctan⁡(Z′′Z′)|Z| = \sqrt{Z'^2 + Z''^2}, \quad \phi = \arctan\left(\frac{Z''}{Z'}\right)∣Z∣=Z′2+Z′′2​,ϕ=arctan(Z′Z′′​)

The phase angle is output in degrees (phase_deg).

Output File Description

Each *_eis.csv contains at least:

  • freq_hz: frequency (Hz)
  • z_real_ohm: real part of impedance (Ω)
  • z_imag_ohm: imaginary part of impedance (Ω)
  • z_mod_ohm: impedance modulus (Ω)
  • phase_deg: phase angle (°)

Subsequent Analysis

  • EIS Plotting: Nyquist and Bode Visualization: quickly review Nyquist/Bode plot quality and trends
  • EIS/DRT Analysis: Mapping Frequency-Domain Impedance to a Distribution of Relaxation Times: perform DRT (Distribution of Relaxation Times) analysis

item.title: In-Situ EIS Extraction: DH Instruments
item.description:
This workflow processes in-situ EIS recordings that contain multiple Freq(Hz),Zre(Ω),Zim(Ω) blocks (e.g., 原位EIS数据参考.txt), automatically splitting them into individual standardized CSV segments. A new segment starts each time a new header row is encountered, making it well-suited for electrochemical degradation and trend analysis.

Required Data Format

Example content:

Segment3(控制电位EIS)
Freq(Hz),Zre(Ω),Zim(Ω)
1E5,2.58944E0,-1.55539E0
7.94328E4,2.71237E0,-1.8413E0
...
Segment6(控制电位EIS)
Freq(Hz),Zre(Ω),Zim(Ω)
1E5,2.59732E0,-1.50046E0
7.94328E4,2.72004E0,-1.76758E0
...

Make sure each EIS segment in the input text contains the following three column headers:

  • Freq(Hz)
  • Zre(Ω)
  • Zim(Ω)

Columns are comma-separated, and every subsequent row should consist of numeric values:

Freq(Hz),Zre(Ω),Zim(Ω)
1E5,2.58944E0,-1.55539E0
7.94328E4,2.71237E0,-1.8413E0
...
  • Segment* labels are optional; the parser does not depend on them.
  • Whenever Freq(Hz),Zre(Ω),Zim(Ω) is encountered, it is treated as a new header.

Procedure

  1. Select a single .txt input file (single-file interaction).
  2. The text is read and split into data blocks at each detected header.
  3. Each block is converted to unified columns: freq_hz,z_real_ohm,z_imag_ohm,z_mod_ohm,phase_deg.
  4. The output directory is named <input_filename>_eis_csv, with files named <input_filename>_eis_001.csv, ....

Output Field Description

  • freq_hz: frequency (Hz, floating-point)
  • z_real_ohm: real part (Ω)
  • z_imag_ohm: imaginary part (Ω)
  • z_mod_ohm: modulus ∣Z∣=Z′2+Z′′2|Z| = \sqrt{Z'^2 + Z''^2}∣Z∣=Z′2+Z′′2​
  • phase_deg: phase angle (°)

Notes

  • Rows with frequency <= 0 or invalid numeric values are filtered out.
  • If a segment contains no usable data, an error is reported for that segment and it is skipped.
  • The output columns are fully compatible with EIS Extraction: CHI Instruments Data Preprocessing, so the files can be used directly with EIS Plotting: Nyquist and Bode Visualization and EIS/DRT Analysis: Mapping Frequency-Domain Impedance to a Distribution of Relaxation Times.

item.title: CV: Coulombic Efficiency and Capacitance Calculation
item.description:
This workflow uses the output data from Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to calculate the charge passed during the forward scan and reverse scan of each cycle via numerical integration, yielding coulombic efficiency and electrode capacitance.

Prerequisites

You must first run Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to complete CV data extraction and obtain Excel files, each containing the Scans_Split worksheet. Note: Output data from Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing is not currently supported.

Procedure

  1. Select the input folder: Use the file picker to select the folder containing the Excel data files output by Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing. This folder typically contains CV extraction results at different scan rates.
  2. The system automatically completes the calculations and generates result files and visualization plots.

Scientific Principles

Charge Calculation

By definition of current, the charge QQQ is the integral of current III over time ttt. For discrete data, numerical integration is performed using the trapezoidal rule:

Q=∫t1t2I(t) dt≈∑k=1N−1I(tk)+I(tk+1)2⋅ΔtQ = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} I(t)\, \mathrm{d}t \approx \sum_{k=1}^{N-1} \frac{I(t_k) + I(t_{k+1})}{2} \cdot \Delta tQ=∫t1​t2​​I(t)dt≈k=1∑N−1​2I(tk​)+I(tk+1​)​⋅Δt

where the time step Δt\Delta tΔt is derived from the sample interval and scan rate:

Δt=ΔEsampleν\Delta t = \frac{\Delta E_{\text{sample}}}{\nu}Δt=νΔEsample​​

Here, ΔEsample\Delta E_{\text{sample}}ΔEsample​ is the sampling potential interval (V), and ν\nuν is the scan rate (V/s).

Coulombic Efficiency

Coulombic efficiency (CE) is defined as the ratio of the charge passed during the reverse scan (reduction process) to the charge passed during the forward scan (oxidation process):

ηCE=QreverseQforward×100%\eta_{\text{CE}} = \frac{Q_{\text{reverse}}}{Q_{\text{forward}}} \times 100\%ηCE​=Qforward​Qreverse​​×100%

This metric reflects the degree of reversibility of the electrode process. For an ideal, fully reversible process, the coulombic efficiency should approach 100%.

Capacitance Calculation

For electrode materials exhibiting capacitive behavior, the capacitance CCC is defined as the ratio of charge to the potential window ΔE\Delta EΔE:

C=QΔE=∫∣I∣ dtEhigh−ElowC = \frac{Q}{\Delta E} = \frac{\int |I|\, \mathrm{d}t}{E_{\text{high}} - E_{\text{low}}}C=ΔEQ​=Ehigh​−Elow​∫∣I∣dt​

where EhighE_{\text{high}}Ehigh​ and ElowE_{\text{low}}Elow​ are the upper and lower limits of the scan potential window, respectively.

Output Files

Upon completion, a Coulombic_Efficiency.xlsx file is generated containing the following two worksheets:

Summary_Stats

Coulombic efficiency and capacitance statistics (mean and standard deviation) grouped by scan rate, used for evaluating the repeatability and stability of the test data.

Detailed_Per_Cycle

Detailed calculation results for each cycle in each file:

Field Description
Q_Forward / Q_Reverse Forward/reverse scan charge (C)
CE (%) Coulombic efficiency
Cap_Forward / Cap_Reverse Forward/reverse scan capacitance (F)
Cap_Avg Average capacitance (F)

Subsequent Analysis

Based on the output of this workflow, you can proceed with pseudocapacitance analysis such as CV/Pseudocapacitance Analysis: b-Value Kinetic Analysis or CV/Cdl: Double-Layer Capacitance and Electrochemically Active Surface Area Analysis.

item.title: EIS Plotting: Nyquist and Bode Visualization
item.description:
Once you have finished extracting EIS data, the natural first step is to plot the results and assess the data quality.

This workflow batch-plots all extracted *_eis.csv files as Nyquist and Bode diagrams, letting you quickly spot sample differences, outliers, and measurement stability. It also exports an Origin project file so you can refine and publish figures later.

Prerequisites

Run EIS Extraction: CHI Instruments Data Preprocessing or In-Situ EIS Extraction: DH Instruments first and make sure the directory already contains standardized *_eis.csv files.

Procedure

  1. Select the input directory: choose the output directory from EIS Extraction: CHI Instruments Data Preprocessing.
  2. The system automatically detects all *_eis.csv files and batch-plots them.
  3. The output directory is the input directory itself; once processing is complete you can view images and project files directly.

What Gets Generated

1) Nyquist Plot

  • x-axis: Z′Z'Z′
  • y-axis: −Z′′-Z''−Z′′
  • Useful for observing charge-transfer impedance, diffusion behavior, and the overall shape before equivalent-circuit fitting

2) Bode Plot

  • Magnitude plot: ∣Z∣|Z|∣Z∣ vs. frequency (log scale)
  • Phase plot: Phase vs. frequency (log scale)
  • Convenient for comparing response mechanisms across different frequency ranges

Output

Each sample produces:

  • *_nyquist_matplotlib.png
  • *_bode_matplotlib.png
  • *_eis_plots.opju (single-sample Origin project)

In addition, a merged file is generated:

  • eis_plots_merged.opju (multi-sample merged Origin project)

Subsequent Analysis

  • EIS/DRT Analysis: Mapping Frequency-Domain Impedance to a Distribution of Relaxation Times: perform DRT analysis on the same set of *_eis.csv files

item.title: CV: Plot the Last Complete Cycle
item.description:
This workflow extracts the last complete cycle at each scan rate from multi-cycle CV data output by Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing, and overlays the steady-state CV curves from different scan rates on a single plot for intuitive comparison of electrochemical response characteristics across scan rates.

Prerequisites

You must first run Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to complete CV data extraction and obtain Excel files, each containing the Scans_Split worksheet.

Procedure

  1. Select the input folder: Use the file picker to select the folder containing the Excel data files output by Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing.
  2. The system automatically extracts the last complete cycle from each file and generates an overlaid CV plot.

Principle

In cyclic voltammetry experiments, the electrode typically reaches an electrochemically stable state after multiple scan cycles. The CV curve from the last cycle is considered to best represent the intrinsic electrochemical behavior of the material at a given scan rate, and is therefore commonly used as the standard data for comparing responses across different scan rates.

Selection of the Last Complete Cycle

The system reads the Scans_Split worksheet and checks whether the last set of scan segments (the last 4 columns) contains complete forward and reverse scan data:

  • If the last cycle is complete (both forward and reverse scans contain data), it is used directly.
  • If the last cycle is incomplete (containing only a unidirectional scan), the system falls back to the penultimate cycle.

Curve Concatenation and Plotting

For each scan rate, the potential–current data from the forward scan and reverse scan are concatenated end-to-end to form a complete, closed CV curve. Curves at different scan rates are distinguished by a colormap, and the legend automatically labels the corresponding scan rate (the display unit—V/s, mV/s, or μV/s—is selected automatically based on the numerical magnitude).

Output

  • Overlaid CV plot (potential versus current), with Potential (V) on the x-axis and Current (A) on the y-axis.
  • The image is saved in PNG format to the input folder.

Subsequent Analysis

Based on visual observation of the last-cycle data, you can proceed with the appropriate analysis path:

  • CV: Coulombic Efficiency and Capacitance Calculation: calculate coulombic efficiency at each scan rate
  • CV/Pseudocapacitance Analysis: b-Value Kinetic Analysis: perform pseudocapacitive b-value kinetic analysis

item.title: EIS/DRT Analysis: Mapping Frequency-Domain Impedance to a Distribution of Relaxation Times
item.description:
If you have already reviewed the Nyquist and Bode plots but want to understand which kinetic process is dominating the response, this workflow is designed for exactly that purpose.

It performs DRT (Distribution of Relaxation Times) analysis on extracted EIS data, mapping frequency-domain impedance information onto a time-constant distribution. This makes it much easier to distinguish different processes visually (e.g., interfacial charge transfer, diffusion-related processes, etc.).

Prerequisites

Run EIS Extraction: CHI Instruments Data Preprocessing or In-Situ EIS Extraction: DH Instruments first and ensure the input consists of standardized EIS CSVs containing freq_hz, z_real_ohm, and z_imag_ohm.

Procedure

You have two options:

  1. Select a directory (batch-process all .csv files in it)
  2. Or select a single .csv file (process one sample only)

The program automatically creates a drt_output directory and outputs results for each sample separately.

Analysis and Fitting Results

Each sample produces the following data files:

  • fit_data.csv: experimental impedance, DRT-reconstructed impedance, and residuals
  • drt_data.csv: τ\tauτ and γ(τ)\gamma(\tau)γ(τ) distribution
  • summary.json: regularization parameters and solver summary (e.g., lambda_value, epsilon)

Along with the following visualization plots:

  • nyquist_fit.png: experimental vs. DRT-fitted Nyquist comparison
  • drt_tau.png: γ\gammaγ–τ\tauτ distribution plot (log-scale x-axis)
  • residuals.png: real/imaginary residual plot
  • *_drt_plots.opju: Origin project (containing Nyquist, DRT, and residual plots)

Principle (Brief)

DRT represents impedance as a superposition of processes with different time constants. The core idea can be written as:

Z(ω)=R∞+∫γ(τ)1+jωτ dln⁡τZ(\omega)=R_\infty + \int \frac{\gamma(\tau)}{1+j\omega\tau} \, d\ln\tauZ(ω)=R∞​+∫1+jωτγ(τ)​dlnτ

Where:

  • The peak positions of γ(τ)\gamma(\tau)γ(τ) reflect the characteristic time scales of different processes
  • The peak area and height relate to the contribution strength of each process

This approach makes it significantly easier to resolve overlapping mechanisms compared to interpreting Nyquist semicircles alone.

FAQ

  • Why are there no results for some samples? The most common reason is missing input columns or invalid values in the data. The program skips these samples and reports the specific error.

Practical Tips

If this is your first time running DRT, it is a good idea to use EIS Plotting: Nyquist and Bode Visualization first to verify that the curves are smooth and free of obvious outliers. Doing so before entering this step typically yields more stable and more interpretable results.

item.title: CV/Pseudocapacitance Analysis: b-Value Kinetic Analysis
item.description:
This workflow uses the output data from Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to calculate the bbb values for both the forward (anodic) and reverse (cathodic) scans by performing power-law fitting on the currents at the midpoint potential across different scan rates, enabling determination of the kinetic control mechanism of the electrode reaction.

Prerequisites

You must first run Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to complete CV data extraction. The input folder should contain CV extraction results (Excel files) at multiple different scan rates to ensure statistical significance of the fitting.

Procedure

  1. Select the input folder: Use the file picker to select the folder containing the CV data at different scan rates output by Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing.
  2. The system automatically extracts midpoint currents, performs fitting calculations, and generates a kinetic analysis plot in log-log coordinates.

Scientific Principles

Power-Law Relationship

In cyclic voltammetry, the peak current (or the current at a specific potential) iii and the scan rate ν\nuν satisfy a power-law relationship:

i=a⋅νbi = a \cdot \nu^bi=a⋅νb

where aaa is a constant and bbb is the kinetic exponent. Taking the logarithm of both sides yields the linear form:

log⁡i=b⋅log⁡ν+log⁡a\log i = b \cdot \log \nu + \log alogi=b⋅logν+loga

Physical Significance of the b Value

The bbb value is used to determine the rate-controlling step of the electrode process:

bbb Value Control Mechanism Physical Significance
b≈0.5b \approx 0.5b≈0.5 Diffusion-controlled Current is limited by the diffusion rate of reactants in solution
b≈1.0b \approx 1.0b≈1.0 Surface-controlled (capacitive behavior) Current is dominated by surface adsorption/desorption processes
0.5<b<1.00.5 < b < 1.00.5<b<1.0 Mixed control Both diffusion and surface processes contribute

Midpoint Potential Selection

This workflow uses the current values at the midpoint EmidE_{\text{mid}}Emid​ of the potential window as the analysis subject:

Emid=Ehigh+Elow2E_{\text{mid}} = \frac{E_{\text{high}} + E_{\text{low}}}{2}Emid​=2Ehigh​+Elow​​

For the last complete cycle in each scan rate file, the absolute values of the current at EmidE_{\text{mid}}Emid​ during the forward scan and reverse scan are extracted separately, denoted as iai_aia​ (anodic current) and ici_cic​ (cathodic current).

Fitting Method

Least-squares linear fitting is performed in the log⁡ν\log \nulogν–log⁡i\log ilogi space to obtain the bbb values and goodness-of-fit R2R^2R2 for the anodic and cathodic processes, respectively.

Output

  • Log-log scatter plot with fitting lines: The x-axis is scan rate ν\nuν (V/s) and the y-axis is current iii (A), both in logarithmic scale. The plot includes anodic (red) and cathodic (blue) data sets with their fitting lines, and the legend annotates the bbb values and R2R^2R2.
  • Data files: Raw data and fitting curve data are exported as separate CSV files.

Subsequent Analysis

  • CV/Cdl: Double-Layer Capacitance and Electrochemically Active Surface Area Analysis: Performs CdlC_{\text{dl}}Cdl​ linear fitting based on midpoint current differences across scan rates to calculate the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA)
  • CV: Coulombic Efficiency and Capacitance Calculation: Evaluates the reversibility of electrode reactions

item.title: CV/Cdl: Double-Layer Capacitance and Electrochemically Active Surface Area Analysis
item.description:
This workflow uses the output data from Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to obtain the double-layer capacitance CdlC_{\text{dl}}Cdl​ through linear fitting of the difference between anodic and cathodic currents at the midpoint potential across different scan rates, which can be further used to calculate the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA).

Prerequisites

You must first run Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to complete CV data extraction. The input folder should contain CV extraction results at multiple different scan rates.

Procedure

  1. Select the input folder: Use the file picker to select the folder containing the CV data at different scan rates output by Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing.
  2. The system automatically calculates ΔI/2\Delta I / 2ΔI/2 values at each scan rate, performs linear fitting, and generates a fitting plot.

Scientific Principles

Determination of Double-Layer Capacitance CdlC_{\text{dl}}Cdl​

In the non-Faradaic potential region, only double-layer charging and discharging occurs at the electrode surface. Under these conditions, the charging current ici_cic​ is proportional to the scan rate ν\nuν:

ic=Cdl⋅νi_c = C_{\text{dl}} \cdot \nuic​=Cdl​⋅ν

In practice, the average of the absolute values of the anodic current iai_aia​ and cathodic current ici_cic​ at the midpoint potential EmidE_{\text{mid}}Emid​ is taken as the approximate double-layer charging current at that scan rate:

ΔI2=∣ia−ic∣2\frac{\Delta I}{2} = \frac{|i_a - i_c|}{2}2ΔI​=2∣ia​−ic​∣​

where EmidE_{\text{mid}}Emid​ is defined as:

Emid=Ehigh+Elow2E_{\text{mid}} = \frac{E_{\text{high}} + E_{\text{low}}}{2}Emid​=2Ehigh​+Elow​​

Linear Fitting

A linear fit is performed with ν\nuν on the x-axis and ΔI/2\Delta I / 2ΔI/2 on the y-axis:

ΔI2=Cdl⋅ν+b\frac{\Delta I}{2} = C_{\text{dl}} \cdot \nu + b2ΔI​=Cdl​⋅ν+b

The slope of the fit yields the double-layer capacitance CdlC_{\text{dl}}Cdl​ (unit: F). Ideally, the intercept bbb should approach zero.

Given the specific capacitance CsC_sCs​ (unit: μF/cm2\mu\text{F/cm}^2μF/cm2) of a particular electrode material in a specific electrolyte, the ECSA can be calculated as:

Output

  • Linear fitting plot: The x-axis is scan rate ν\nuν (V/s), and the y-axis is ΔI/2\Delta I / 2ΔI/2 (A). The plot includes experimental data points (scatter) and the least-squares fitting line, annotated with the CdlC_{\text{dl}}Cdl​ value and R2R^2R2.
